claims.reason: inspectCodexIntegration can throw from journal inspection at doctor.ts:155, escaping runDoctor before later independent checks; the CLI fallback emits only generic stderr and no DoctorReport.

A selected profile TOML parse error is swallowed at route-diagnostics.ts:68 and collapses into profile-unavailable, losing the distinction from an absent or invalid selection despite the root config-invalid classification.
Root and selected-profile reads share one catch at route-diagnostics.ts:124-138, so a profile read failure is reported as config-unreadable and discards valid root evidence.
This independently reports the same uncaught Codex integration probe at doctor.ts:155 and the same loss of the aggregate doctor report; it is a duplicate root.
The managed-chrome login path calls secureFile, whose statSync can throw outside a per-probe guard at doctor.ts:144-151, aborting the report before subsequent checks.

roots.title: Uncaught Codex integration probe aborts the aggregate doctor report
roots.trigger: The Codex integration journal is unreadable or invalid so inspectCodexIntegration throws during runDoctor.
roots.fix: Catch this individual probe, append a bounded codex error check, and continue the existing service, proxy, tunnel, and connector checks.

roots.title: Selected profile failures lose their identity and root configuration evidence
roots.trigger: A requested profile is malformed or cannot be read while the root config.toml is valid.
roots.fix: Guard root and profile reads separately, preserve valid root diagnostics, and emit distinct stable profile parse/read issue codes.

roots.title: Managed-chrome login permission probe can abort doctor without a check
roots.trigger: The login state or verification marker changes or becomes non-stat-able between existence and permission checks, causing secureFile statSync to throw.
roots.fix: Wrap the complete login probe in a per-probe guard and append a bounded login error check when filesystem inspection fails.
